title: Open Legend — Art Direction, Round 03
status: Five new illustrated comparisons, five returning pixel-art comparisons, two favorite benchmarks. No popularity ranking implied.

entries.title: Hades
entries.focus: Angled environments, sculpted shapes, distinctive silhouettes
entries.borrow: Compare ordinary world-character size with the richness of stone, water and vegetation. Test the overall finish you explicitly like.
entries.caution: Bold stylization and supernatural architecture are not requirements for Open Legend. This is an art-direction reference, not a pixel-art production recipe.
entries.question: What do you most want to carry over: the world artwork, character shape, colors, angled camera, or the complete combination?

images.label: Elysium · water, vegetation and gameplay-scale character

entries.note: You explicitly said you really like Hades. This new rating can separate the aspects you like.

entries.title: Hades II
entries.medium: Illustrated hybrid presentation; not pixel art
entries.focus: Detailed portraits paired with smaller world characters
entries.borrow: Compare the Crossroads gameplay scene with the dialogue image. This directly tests your openness to richer profiles alongside readable world avatars.
entries.caution: The dialogue image is official Early Access media, not a claim about the current build. Judge its large portrait separately from the small world figure.
entries.question: Would this split—readable clothing in the world, expressive face and body detail in a profile—meet your character-detail goal?

entries.title: Octopath Traveler II
entries.focus: Warm fire, cool night, miniature people
entries.borrow: Campfire light makes a small group in a huge wilderness feel intimate.
entries.caution: Previously reviewed, included deliberately for comparison with Hades. Your earlier response remains valid; this is not presented as a new discovery.
entries.question: Compared directly with Hades, is this pixel-based treatment still desirable, or does the small RPG figure feel too simplified?
entries.note: Round one: like. I like the art generally though I feel like the style of the people and some of the assets in particular feel a little bit outdated. They feel a little bit like they are from 10 years ago, which they are. I like the overall vibe and the lighting especially, but I would like something that feels a little bit more modern. I want this to appeal to Gen Z and Gen Alpha.
entries.reuse: Visual reference only. Artwork remains at credited hosts; no production reuse rights acquired.

entries.title: Eastward
entries.focus: Lush clutter and a world with history
entries.borrow: Props, overgrowth, and worn surfaces imply lives beyond the camera.
entries.caution: Previously reviewed, included deliberately for comparison with Hades. Your earlier response remains valid; this is not presented as a new discovery.
entries.question: Keep the environmental detail, but would you prefer Hades-like world characters and larger profile portraits?
entries.note: Round one: like. I like the vibrant colors, the level of detail, and the fact that the building is pretty detailed. I think the character bodies could be more detailed. I don't want my characters to have Pokemon-style bodies that are very undetailed. I want the characters to be detailed enough that they can have visible armor and clothing and, ideally, their faces, skin tone, fashion, etc., are somewhat recognizable. I want pretty detailed pixels.
entries.reuse: Visual reference only. Artwork remains at credited hosts; no production reuse rights acquired.

entries.note: Round one: maybe. The character has a good deal of detail. You can see his gear and everything. That's pretty solid. I do like the level of detail on the character. The environment itself is also quite nice and detailed although it does feel a little bit too cartoony and painted.

entries.note: Round one: maybe. Very solid environment. I like the detail and the aesthetic. I don't know about adopting this particular aesthetic but I do like the quality of the aesthetic. The character also has some detail. It is not super detailed but could be more detailed. The environment is nice.
